acceptanceCriteria: Primary or discovered default checkout is rejected before a close decision or cleanup receipt is written.
A dedicated linked worktree on a non-default branch retains the existing close and exact cleanup behavior.
The rejection identifies the discovered default branch or primary checkout and gives the required next action without hardcoding main.
Regression coverage proves rejected close leaves no partial governance state and existing cleanup receipts remain valid.
goal: Reject unsafe ordinary close contexts before writing close or cleanup evidence, while preserving the dedicated linked-worktree lifecycle.
intent: Prevent ordinary Work Item closure from binding cleanup to the repository primary or discovered default checkout, which creates an impossible cleanup obligation after merge.
